hypothesis: The GNN partitioner is under-trained at the fixed 100 epochs / lr=1e-3 with a contrastive objective that never sees wirelength, so embeddings are noisy and tier assignment is near-random for large designs; increasing training epochs (100 -> 300) lets the contrastive objective actually separate connected cells, giving a more wirelength-aware partition that shortens both same-tier and cross-tier critical connections and reduces TNS.
analysis: Hypothesis partly held: longer training helped ariane133-ng45 (dTNS -13.0%, dWNS -5.2%) and bp-ng45 (dWNS -6.3%), consistent with better-separated embeddings yielding more wirelength-aware tiers. But bp_fe-ng45 was mixed (dWNS +6.1%, dTNS -2.7%), and all scores are negative overall (total -0.121), so the effect is not robustly beneficial. Overflow ~101-150 suggests congestion may be confounding. Next step: sweep epochs (100/200/300) with a wirelength-aware contrastive term and report per-case WNS/TNS plus overflow, to confirm the mechanism rather than just epoch count.
